# sec-filing-ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md (both PROPOSED; the spec's §2.2 puts O2 and O3 out of its own scope, and they come from your partner's words).
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). uv workspace with packages sec-edgar-client, sec-edgar-download, sec-edgar-index-ingest and sec-edgar-ingest (scaffolds only).

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 requests/second (SEC full-index and daily-index directories); measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks for the full history at 3 requests/second (index row count × request rate); measured by Stages 2 and 6 |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until submissions are on disk; measured by Stages 3 and 7 |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Index core
      Objective: Ingest one real closed quarter's quarterly master index and the open quarter's daily master indexes to date into one filing-index table.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: the workspace scaffold only
      Produces: the filing-index table for that slice; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — the table holds that quarter's rows and the open quarter's daily rows, and its row count matches the source files; findings record the elapsed time, bytes downloaded, rows and SEC requests of the real run
      Leaves out: raw retention, manifest, replay and versioned publication (Stage 4); full history and per-file resume (Stage 5); shared request budget (Stage 6); reconciliation and withdrawals (Stage 8); full validation suite (Stage 9); scheduling, deployment and monitoring (Stage 10)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submissions core
      Objective: Download the submissions that the Stage 1 closed quarter's index rows name.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: that quarter's submissions on disk; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-2-findings.md
      Exit: O2 — every submission named by that quarter's rows is on disk or listed as failed with its reason; findings record the elapsed time, bytes, files and SEC requests, and a full-history projection from them
      Leaves out: raw retention, manifest and replay (Stage 4); full history and resume (Stage 6); shared request budget (Stage 6); full validation suite (Stage 9); scheduling (Stage 10)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K core
      Objective: Pick the 10-K and 8-K filings out of Stage 2's submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's submissions on disk
      Produces: extracted main documents for that quarter's 10-K and 8-K filings; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-3-findings.md
      Exit: O3 — every 10-K and 8-K in that quarter has its main document extracted or is listed as failed, with counts by form; findings record the elapsed time and output volume
      Leaves out: replay of extraction from stored bytes (Stage 4); full history (Stage 7); full validation suite (Stage 9); scheduling (Stage 10)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Raw retention, manifest and replay
      Objective: Retain original bytes with provenance and make parsing and extraction replayable without SEC requests, with versioned per-quarter publication of the index table (background spec R6, R9, §4.5, §4.6).
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: Stages 1–3 code and outputs
      Produces: hash-addressed raw index files; a source manifest; per-quarter index generations behind one active pointer; extraction replayable from stored submissions
      Exit: O1 — a parser-version change rebuilds the Stage 1 slice from stored bytes with zero SEC requests and no duplicate rows, and readers see only the generation the pointer names; O3 — re-extraction of the Stage 3 quarter from stored submissions makes zero SEC requests and yields the same document set
      Leaves out: reconciliation and withdrawal approval (Stage 8); fault-injection and historical-format fixtures (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Index full history
      Objective: Backfill the index table over the full quarterly range and catch daily ingestion up across quarter boundaries, resumable per source file (background spec §4.2).
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 4's manifest and publication
      Produces: a filing-index table covering every quarter in the range plus daily rows to date; a coverage report
      Exit: O1 — every quarter in the range is published or listed as a gap in the report; a run killed mid-backfill resumes without re-downloading completed files; recorded elapsed time and volume of the full run
      Leaves out: shared request budget (Stage 6); reconciliation (Stage 8); golden fixtures across historical formats (Stage 9); scheduling (Stage 10)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Submissions full history under one request budget
      Objective: Download every submission the full index names, resumably, with all SEC traffic sharing one request budget (background spec R8, §4.3).
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 5's full index table; Stage 2's findings for the projection
      Produces: the full submissions archive; a shared request budget all SEC traffic goes through
      Exit: O2 — every named submission is on disk or listed as pending or failed; request logs show index ingestion and the bulk download running together never exceed the combined target; recorded total time, bytes and requests
      Leaves out: full validation suite (Stage 9); scheduling (Stage 10)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: 10-K and 8-K full history
      Objective: Extend Stage 3's handling over the full submissions archive.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 6's submissions archive; Stage 4's replayable extraction
      Produces: extracted main documents for every 10-K and 8-K in the archive
      Exit: O3 — every 10-K and 8-K has its main document extracted or is listed as failed, with counts by form and year; recorded elapsed time and volume
      Leaves out: full validation suite (Stage 9); scheduling (Stage 10)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Reconciliation and withdrawals
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes and apply additions, changes and withdrawals under the background spec's precedence and approval rules (R7, R10, §4.4).
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 4's generations and pointer; Stage 5's full index table
      Produces: per-generation change reports; withdrawal approvals bound to source hashes
      Exit: O1 — a changed quarterly snapshot produces a change report; a closed-quarter removal stays in the active table until approved against that hash; open-quarter absence never removes a row
      Leaves out: scheduled weekly runs (Stage 10)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 9: Validation suite
      Objective: Bring CI to the background spec's test standard (§6, §4.6 fixtures) across the index, submissions and extraction paths.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 1–8
      Produces: committed fixtures and fault-injection tests run in CI without SEC access
      Exit: O1 — fixtures cover each historical index format in the backfilled range, and malformed, HTML and conflicting-duplicate inputs fail closed; O2 — throttling, access-denial and resume cases pass on mocked responses; O3 — extraction fixtures pass for 10-K and 8-K; CI makes zero network requests
      Leaves out: Azure integration tests (Stage 10)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 10: Scheduling, deployment and operations
      Objective: Run daily ingestion and weekly reconciliation on a schedule on the chosen platform, with monitoring, alerts and runbooks (background ADR; spec R4, §4.7–§4.9, §7, §8).
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 1–9
      Produces: deployed scheduled runs, alerts and runbooks
      Exit: O1 — two consecutive scheduled daily runs and one scheduled reconciliation are recorded in durable reports; O2 — the scheduled daily run downloads that day's new submissions; O3 — the scheduled daily run extracts that day's new 10-K and 8-K documents; an injected failure raises an alert
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming
